being non-zero when deciding whether or not to attempt to fix a page
fault vian the fast path.  Originally
non-zero if and only if A/D bits were disabled by _KVM_ (including not
being supported by hardware)
column2: but that hasn't been true since nVMX was

column1: fixed to honor EPTP12's A/D enabling
column2: i.e. since KVM allowed L1 to cause

column1: KVM to not use A/D bits while running L2 despite KVM using them while
running L1.
In other words
column2: don't attempt the fast path just because EPT is enabled.

column1: Note
column2: attempting the fast path for all !PRESENT faults can ""fix"" a very

column1: _VERY_ tiny percentage of faults out of mmu_lock by detecting that the
fault is spurious
column2: i.e. has been fixed by a different vCPU

column1: odds of that happening are vanishingly small.  E.g. booting an 8-vCPU VM
gets less than 10 successes out of 30k+ faults
the more favorable scenarios.  Disabling dirty logging can likely lead to
a rash of collisions between vCPUs for some workloads that operate on a
common set of pages
column2: but penalizing _all_ !PRESENT faults for that one

column1: case is unlikely to be a net positive
column2: not to mention that that problem

column1: is best solved by not zapping in the first place.
The number of spurious faults does scale with the number of vCPUs
255-vCPU VM using TDP ""jumps"" to ~60 spurious faults detected in the fast
path (again out of 30k)
column2: but that's all of 0.2% of faults.  Using legacy

column1: shadow paging does get more spurious faults
column2: and a few more detected out

column1: of mmu_lock
column2: but the percentage goes _down_ to 0.08% (and that's ignoring

column1: faults that are reflected into the guest)
purely due to the sheer number of faults observed.
On the other hand
column2: getting a ""negative"" in the fast path takes in the

column1: neighborhood of 150-250 cycles.  So while it is tempting to keep/extend
the current behavior
column2: such a change needs to come with hard numbers

column1: showing that it's actually a win in the grand scheme
that matter.
